t.6.20.1: Having seen those leaders of the monkey troops described by Śuka, and his own brother Vibhīṣaṇa standing near Rāma,
t.6.20.3: Somewhat agitated at heart and with anger risen in him, Rāvaṇa, at the end of their account, rebuked those two heroes, Śuka and Sāraṇa.
t.6.20.2: And Lakṣmaṇa of great valor, the right arm of Rāma, and Sugrīva of terrible prowess, king of all the monkeys.
t.6.20.4: Enraged, he spoke harsh words in a voice choked with anger to Śuka and Sāraṇa, the two who stood bowed before him with downcast faces.
t.6.20.5: It is surely not fitting for ministers who depend on him for their livelihood to speak what is displeasing to a king, the lord who has power to restrain and to favor.
t.6.20.6: Is it indeed fitting for you two to speak, at so inappropriate a moment, in praise of hostile enemies who are advancing for battle?
t.6.20.7: In vain have you two attended upon teachers, gurus and elders, since the essence of the treatises on kingship, by which one ought to live, has not been grasped by you.
t.6.20.8: Whether it has been grasped or not truly understood, it is merely the burden of knowledge that is being carried. Yoked to such foolish ministers as these, it is only by good fortune that I still hold on.
t.6.20.9: Is there truly no fear of death in you, that you dare speak harsh words to me, to me whose tongue, as I rule, dispenses good and ill?
t.6.20.10: Trees in the forest may still stand even after fire has touched them, but offenders touched by the king's displeasure do not survive.
t.6.20.11: I would slay these two wicked ones who praise the enemy's side, were it not that my anger is softened by their former services to me.
t.6.20.12: Begone, go away from here, out of my presence! I do not wish to kill you two, for I remember the services you have done me. Ungrateful and turned away from affection for me, those two are as good as slain already.
t.6.20.13: Thus addressed, both Śuka and Sāraṇa, filled with shame, hailed Rāvaṇa with cries of victory and departed.
t.6.20.14: Then Daśagrīva said to Mahodara, who stood near him: "Quickly bring before me spies who are skilled in policy."
t.6.20.15: Then the spies, hastening at the king's command, arrived and stood before him with joined palms, having honored him with blessings of victory.
t.6.20.16: Then Rāvaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, spoke these words to them, his spies, who were trustworthy, brave, devoted, and free from fear.
t.6.20.17: Go from here and examine Rāma's resolve, and find out who are his intimates in counsel, those who have joined him out of affection.
t.6.20.18: How does he sleep, how does he keep watch, and what else will he do? Having learned all this thoroughly and in full detail, you must return.
t.6.20.19: An enemy whose designs are known through a spy is, by wise lords of the earth, engaged in battle and repelled with very little effort.
t.6.20.20: Then those spies, delighted, said "So be it," and having circumambulated the lord of the Rākṣasas, they went to where Rāma was with Lakṣmaṇa.
t.6.20.21: Having gone near Mount Suvela, they, remaining concealed, saw Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa together with Sugrīva and Vibhīṣaṇa.
t.6.20.22: But those rākṣasas, while they were there, were spotted by chance by the righteous-souled Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, and were seized.
t.6.20.23: But they, harassed by the valiant monkeys of swift prowess, returned again to Laṅkā, panting and bereft of their senses.
t.6.20.24: Then those spies, mighty night-rangers ever roaming abroad, approached Daśagrīva and reported to him the one of terrible strength who was dwelling near Mount Suvela.
